# 1 Samuel Chapter 4 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 133v–134r | **Source Image:** 1SA_004_page_001.jpg, 1SA_004_page_002.jpg

---

**1** And the word of Samuel came to all Israel. And Israel went out to meet the Philistines in battle, and they encamped beside Ebenezer, and the Philistines encamped at Aphek.

**2** And the Philistines drew up in battle array against Israel, and the battle spread, and Israel was struck down before the Philistines, who struck down about four thousand men on the field of battle.

**3** And when the people came to the camp, the elders of Israel said, "Why has the LORD struck us today before the Philistines? Let us bring to ourselves from Shiloh the ark of the covenant of the LORD, that it may come into our midst and save us from the hand of our enemies."

**4** So the people sent to Shiloh, and they carried from there the ark of the covenant of the LORD of hosts, who is enthroned upon the cherubim. And the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the ark of the covenant of God.

**5** And when the ark of the covenant of the LORD came into the camp, all Israel raised a great shout, and the earth resounded.

**6** And the Philistines heard the sound of the shout and said, "What is this great shout in the camp of the Hebrews?" And they learned that the ark of the LORD had come into the camp.

**7** And the Philistines were afraid, for they said, "God has come into the camp." And they said, "Woe to us! For nothing like this has happened before.

**8** Woe to us! Who will deliver us from the hand of these mighty gods? These are the gods who struck Egypt with every kind of plague in the wilderness.

**9** Take courage and be men, O Philistines, lest you become servants to the Hebrews as they have served you. Be men and fight!"

**10** So the Philistines fought, and Israel was struck down, and every man fled to his tent. And the slaughter was very great, and there fell from Israel thirty thousand foot soldiers.

**11** And the ark of God was captured, and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, died.

**12** And a man of Benjamin ran from the battle line and came to Shiloh that same day, with his garments torn and earth upon his head.

**13** And when he arrived, there was Eli, sitting on his seat by the side of the road, watching, for his heart trembled for the ark of God. And when the man came to report in the city, all the city cried out.

**14** And Eli heard the sound of the outcry and said, "What is this sound of tumult?" And the man hurried and came and reported to Eli.

**15** Now Eli was ninety-eight years old, and his eyes were set so that he could not see.

**16** And the man said to Eli, "I am the one who has come from the battle line; I fled from the battle today." And he said, "What happened, my son?"

**17** And the messenger answered and said, "Israel has fled before the Philistines, and there has also been a great slaughter among the people, and your two sons also, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead, and the ark of God has been captured."

**18** And when he mentioned the ark of God, Eli fell backward from his seat beside the gate, and his neck was broken and he died, for the man was old and heavy. And he had judged Israel forty years.

**19** Now his daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas, was pregnant and about to give birth. And when she heard the report that the ark of God was captured and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead, she bowed down and gave birth, for her labor pains came upon her.

**20** And at the time of her dying, the women attending her said, "Do not be afraid, for you have borne a son." But she did not answer, nor did she take it to heart.

**21** And she named the child Ichabod, saying, "The glory has departed from Israel," because of the capture of the ark of God and because of her father-in-law and her husband.

**22** And she said, "The glory has departed from Israel, for the ark of God has been captured."

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

1. **4:1 — textual division**: The Leningrad Codex places "And the word of Samuel came to all Israel" at the opening of chapter 4. The LXX and 4QSam-a traditions treat this as the conclusion of chapter 3.

2. **4:4 — "enthroned upon the cherubim"**: The Hebrew יֹשֵׁב הַכְּרוּבִים is a divine title describing the LORD seated upon the cherubim atop the ark's mercy seat. LOGOS renders the participle as a title rather than a simple verb.

3. **4:8 — "in the wilderness"**: The Philistines conflate the Egyptian plagues with wilderness events — an authentic detail reflecting their imperfect knowledge of Israelite tradition. The plural "gods" reflects their polytheistic perspective.

4. **4:18 — "forty years"**: This notice places Eli within the Judges framework. The number forty is a conventional period in biblical chronology, marking a generation.

5. **4:21 — Ichabod** (אִי־כָבוֹד): The name means "no glory" or "where is the glory?" The prefix אִי functions as a negation. The dying mother's naming act — like Rachel's naming of Ben-oni — is a theological statement: the ark's capture means the departure of divine glory from Israel.

6. **4:19-22 — order of grief**: The wife of Phinehas receives the news in a descending order of theological significance: the ark (first and last), her father-in-law, her husband. The ark's capture, not personal loss, drives the naming.

— LOGOS
